trial_court: Court of learned Senior Sub Judge, Kullu, District Kullu, H.P. in Civil Suit No.58 of 1988
case_name: Chaitru & Another vs Kali Dass & Others
facts_of_case: Plaintiffs filed a suit for declaration that they are owners-in-possession of 2/3rd share in the property left by deceased Sh. Lebhu and entitled to remain in possession with consequential relief of injunction.

legal_principles.principle: A substantial question of law need not necessarily be a substantial question of law of general importance.
legal_principles.held: The phrase substantial question of law as it was employed in the last clause of the then existing Section 110 of the C.P.C. (since omitted by the Amendment Act, 1973) came up for consideration and Their Lordships held that it did not mean a substantial question of general importance but a substantial question of law which was involved in the case as between the parties.
cited_cases: Guran Ditta & Anr. Vs. T. Ram Ditta
Rimmalapudi Subba Rao Vs. Noony Veeraju
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in determining whether a second appeal shall be heard

legal_principles.principle: A substantial question of law is one that is fairly arguable, where there is room for difference of opinion on it or where the Court thought it necessary to deal with that question at some length and discuss alternative views.
legal_principles.held: When a question of law is fairly arguable, where there is room for difference of opinion on it or where the Court thought it necessary to deal with that question at some length and discuss alternative views, then the question would be a substantial question of law.
cited_cases: Rimmalapudi Subba Rao Vs. Noony Veeraju
Sir Chunilal V. Mehta & Sons Ltd. Vs. The Century Spinning and Manufacuring Co., Ltd.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in determining whether a second appeal shall be heard
